chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
question_text: By spinning eggs on a table top, how will you distinguish a hard-boiled egg from a raw egg?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 7 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The reason
lines: A raw egg has liquid inside. When spun,
the liquid is thrown outward, so the
raw egg has the larger moment of
steps.margin_note: Say WHY the raw egg’s I is larger — the fluid moves outward. The inequality alone is half the reason.
steps.why: The boiled egg is solid and spins as one piece. The raw egg’s fluid lags and spreads outward, putting mass farther from the axis.
common_mistakes: Writing the inequality the wrong way round.

recall.must_convey: That the raw egg has liquid inside, so its moment of inertia is larger when spun.
accept: raw egg has fluid thrown outward
I of raw is greater than I of boiled
raw egg lo liquid untundi I ekkuva

steps.label: The test
lines: Spin both with the same effort. Since
Iω is what the spin gives each egg,
The slower, wobbling one is raw.
steps.margin_note: End with the observable: which egg does what. The examiner marks the test, not just the theory.
steps.why: For the same angular momentum, ω = L/I — the larger I of the raw egg buys a smaller ω. The internal fluid friction also keeps stealing its rotation, which is the wobble.
common_mistakes: Describing the difference in I but never saying which egg visibly spins faster.

recall.must_convey: That the boiled egg spins faster and the raw egg spins slower, which is the test.
accept: raw egg is slower and wobbles
reject: raw egg has fluid thrown outward
